Omni-Agent: enterprise AI platform for Agentic QA and document intelligence.

A production-oriented platform for document intelligence, Agentic QA workflows, RAG, versioned artifacts, asynchronous workers, and evaluation loops.

View GitHub Back to projects
Context

The problem is not just RAG. It is governing the workflow around RAG.

Omni-Agent is designed as an enterprise console where Knowledge Builder and Agentic QA workflows can live under project-level boundaries. The hard part is not only calling an LLM. The hard part is making documents, versions, artifacts, jobs, chunks, vector records, and evaluation traces behave like a reliable product surface.

The case is intentionally framed as a backend control-plane project: Django owns domain state, worker services perform technical jobs, and result envelopes return evidence that can be stored, reviewed, retried, or indexed.

Architecture

Control plane, workers, artifacts, and retrieval are separated.

Project consoleReact UI for documents, versions, preview, jobs, and review actions.
Django APIDomain models, permissions, jobs, source-of-truth state, and presigned artifact access.
Stateless workersOCR, chunking, document conversion, and indexing commands via queue/result envelopes.
RAG layerChunks, vector DB sync, retrieval traces, and Agentic QA workflows.

The important boundary is that technical workers do not secretly own product state. They receive commands and return results; the API decides what a DocumentVersion means and when it becomes committed.

Core modeling

DocumentVersion and ProcessingArtifact make AI output auditable.

The document flow is modeled around versions and artifacts: source file, OCR markdown, parsed document JSON, enhanced OCR, committed text, chunk artifacts, and chunk-version mappings. This makes RAG traceability easier because every retrieval unit can be connected back to a committed document version.

This model is more verbose than a simple "upload file → embed text" flow, but it gives better control over review, rollback, preview, reprocessing, and debugging.

Product decisions

Engineering decisions worth discussing in interviews.

Django as the AI control plane

Context
AI products need strong ownership, permissions, migrations, admin, auditability, and long-lived domain state.
Decision
Use Django/DRF for the control plane and keep heavy model/data tasks behind workers or service clients.
Trade-off
Not the fastest runtime for every request, but much stronger for domain governance, admin visibility, and data integrity.

Stateless document worker boundary

Context
Document OCR, chunking, and artifact generation are CPU/GPU-heavy and should not own product semantics.
Decision
Keep omni-doc-processor as a technical worker: receive typed commands, publish result envelopes, and let the API own domain state.
Trade-off
More contract design upfront, but fewer hidden state transitions and cleaner retry/replay behavior.

Versioned artifacts before vector sync

Context
RAG workflows break down when source documents, OCR text, chunks, and vector records drift independently.
Decision
Model DocumentVersion, ProcessingArtifact, Chunk, and ChunkVersion explicitly before syncing to the vector database.
Trade-off
More schema work, but better traceability, rollback, comparison, and source-of-truth control.
